title: Compatibility Attestation Orchestrator — cross-version compatibility + perf acceptance
creator: Priya Desai
description: Build an orchestration layer (Compatibility Attestation Orchestrator) that generates a deterministic release "attestation" score combining: binary and API compatibility probes, end-to-end smoke acceptance, targeted perf-regression microbenchmarks, and model-output QA checks. The attestation is used as a deterministic gate in the release pipeline to allow automated staged rollouts or to halt and create an incident if thresholds are violated.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator produces a reproducible attestation JSON with a score and per-check details for every release candidate
Attestation integrates into CI such that merges to release branch trigger attestation runs and gate evaluation
Attestation policy supports configurable thresholds per channel (canary, stable, LTS) and emits pass/fail and confidence band
Automated creation of a rollback ticket or canary hold when attestation fails
Attestation runtime completes within configurable SLA (default 45 minutes) for typical candidate builds
implementation_notes: Compatibility probes will run kernel-level ABI checks for serving runtime + lightweight API contract tests against a pinned client shim
Perf gating uses representative microbenchmarks derived from production histograms (90th/99th token latencies, tail KV cache hit scenarios)
Model-output QA uses a small curated 'golden evaluation set' with fuzzy similarity scoring to detect semantic regressions rather than exact match
Orchestrator will compute a weighted score: compatibility(40%), perf(30%), smoke/e2e(20%), qa(10%) — weights configurable per channel
To limit cost we sample a subset of integration matrices based on change impact analysis (file diff + affected subsystems) instead of exhaustive matrix runs
Decision to favor deterministic, debuggable failures over overly noisy heuristics to reduce false positives — conservative thresholding for LTS channel
